title: Rational Neural Networks have Expressivity Advantages
claim: The proposed learnable activation converges faster and reaches higher final accuracy than standard fixed activations across training settings.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend below, zoomed inset in right panel
description: The crop has two parts. At the top is a caption and a results table (Table 2) of CIFAR-10 top-1 accuracy for VGG4 and VGG8 under a strengthened training recipe. Rows are activations (GELU, ReLU, Swish, LeakyReLU, Rational 1, Rational 2). Columns are accuracy without GroupNorm, accuracy with GroupNorm, and time. Green and orange cell highlights mark the best and second-best results. Below the table are two line plots of test accuracy against epoch. The left plot is 'VGG4 plain', where the purple Rational curve stays highest while ReLU and LeakyReLU degrade late in training. The right plot is 'VGG4 boosted (no GN)', where the brown and purple Rational curves lead and a zoomed inset shows the final gap. A shared colored legend runs along the bottom, and shaded bands show standard deviation.
caption: CIFAR-10 test-accuracy score curves for VGG4 in the plain setting (left) and the boosted setting without GroupNorm (right). Curves show mean across five seeds with ±1 standarddeviation shading. Rational converges earlier and to a better final accuracy than the fixed activations in both settings.
abstract: We study neural networks with trainable low-degree rational activation functions and show that they are more expressive and parameter-efficient than modern piecewise-linear and smooth activations such as ELU, LeakyReLU, LogSigmoid, PReLU, ReLU, SELU, CELU, Sigmoid, SiLU, Mish, Softplus, Tanh, Softmin, Softmax, and LogSoftmax. For an error target of $\varepsilon>0$, we establish approximation-theoretic separations: Any network built from standard fixed activations can be uniformly approximated on compact domains by a rational-activation network with only $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$ overhead in size, while the converse provably requires $Î©(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ parameters in the worst case. This exponential gap persists at the level of full networks and extends to gated activations and transformer-style nonlinearities. In practice, rational activations integrate seamlessly into standard architectures and training pipelines, allowing rationals to match or outperform fixed activations under identical architectures and optimizers.
